title_ar: تشمل إقامة محاضرات ودروس وحلقات إفتاء.. الشيخ الددو في رحلة دعوية إلى ولاية داخلت انواذيبو الموريتانية
title_en: Taking In Public Lectures, Classes and Fatwa Sessions — Sheikh al-Dedew on a Da'wah Tour to the Mauritanian Region of Dakhlet Nouadhibou
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء و رئيس جمعية المستقبل وعضو مجلس أمناء الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين محاضرة علمية بعنوان: "عوامل قوة الأمة"، ضمن سلسلة محاضرات ودروس تحتضنها العاصمة الاقتصادية لموريتانيا ولاية داخلت نواذيبو التي تبعد عن العاصمة انواكشوط 470 كلم.

وتأتي هذه الفعالية ضمن رحلة دعوية في الولاية نظمتها جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم يومي 25 و 26 يونيو الجاري، وتشمل الرحلة إقامة سلسلة من المحاضرات والدروس وحلقات الإفتاء.

وهذه أبرز المحاضرات حسب التسلسل الزمني :-

ففي مقاطعة الشامي:

* المحاضرة الأولى: "الكسب الحلال" في جامع الفرقان بمقاطعة الشامي التي كانت مفتتح الرحلة الدعوية.

* حلقة إفتاء خاصة بالمنقبين عن الذهب والعاملين في مجال التنقيب، حيث أجاب الشيخ الددو على أسئلة الحضور.

وفي مقاطعة انواذيبو:

* محاضرة في مسجد قباء عن "نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومقتضياتها".

* محاضرة بعنوان: "كيف نصلي صلاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم؟" في مسجد الرضوان. - الجهة المنظمة جمعية الفرقان للثقافة والتربية.

* محاضرة بعنوان: "عوامل قوة الأمة" في جامع أبي بكر الصديق.

* "فضل عشر ذي الحجة" الجهة المنظمة الجمعية النسوية لمكافحة الفقر والأمية.

* واجب الفتاة المسلمة في نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم - الجهة المنظمة جمعية الفتاة للتوعية والتربية.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew — head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, president of the al-Mustaqbal Association, and a member of the board of trustees of the International Union of Muslim Scholars — delivered a scholarly lecture entitled "The Factors of the Ummah's Strength", as part of a series of lectures and classes hosted by Mauritania's economic capital, the region of Dakhlet Nouadhibou, which lies 470 km from the capital Nouakchott.

This event comes as part of a da'wah tour in the region organised by the al-Mustaqbal Association for Da'wah, Culture and Education on 25 and 26 June of this month; the tour takes in a series of lectures, classes and fatwa sessions.

These are the principal lectures, in chronological order:

In the district of Chami:

* The first lecture: "Lawful Earning", at the al-Furqan congregational mosque in the district of Chami, which opened the da'wah tour.

* A fatwa session specifically for gold prospectors and those working in prospecting, in which Sheikh al-Dedew answered the questions of those present.

And in the district of Nouadhibou:

* A lecture at the Quba mosque on "Coming to the Prophet's Aid, God Bless Him and Grant Him Peace, and What That Requires".

* A lecture entitled "How Do We Pray the Prayer of the Prophet, God Bless Him and Grant Him Peace?", at the al-Ridwan mosque. — Organised by the al-Furqan Association for Culture and Upbringing.

* A lecture entitled "The Factors of the Ummah's Strength", at the Abu Bakr al-Siddiq congregational mosque.

* "The Merit of the Ten Days of Dhu al-Hijjah", organised by the Women's Association for Combating Poverty and Illiteracy.

* The Duty of the Muslim Young Woman in Coming to the Aid of the Prophet, God Bless Him and Grant Him Peace — organised by the al-Fatat Association for Awareness and Upbringing.

flags.arabic: نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومقتضياتها
flags.context: the announced title of one of the lectures
options: coming to the Prophet's aid and what that requires
defending the Prophet and its requirements
supporting the Prophet and what it entails
flags.note: nuṣrah is not in the glossary. In Mauritanian usage of this period the word is tied to the response to insults against the Prophet, so 'defending' is close to the practical sense, but nuṣrah is wider (love, emulation, transmission of the sunnah) and 'defending' would narrow it. Left as 'coming to the aid of', which is the plain sense, with the narrower reading recorded here. Lecture titles are being reported by the site's news desk, not given by the Sheikh in these words.

translator_notes: This is a news report published by the site, not a text by the Sheikh; the only thing attributed to him is his delivering the lectures. Lecture titles are rendered in English with the Arabic preserved in body_ar.
الكسب الحلال is rendered 'lawful earning'. ḥalāl has entered normal English and is not bracketed here, in line with the house rule on naturalised terms.
Mauritanian place names are given in the French-based spellings used officially in Mauritania (Nouadhibou, Nouakchott, Chami), which is how an English-language reader will find them on a map.
The CMS timestamp (30 June 2022) is four days after the tour it reports (25-26 June), so it is a publication date. It is the date of the report and has not been marked a bulk upload.
